title: How the implant prevents pregnancy
answer: The implant is one or two small, soft rods placed under the skin of your upper arm. They slowly release a hormone called progestin. This hormone thickens the mucus at the opening of the womb so sperm cannot get through, and it can also stop eggs from being released. It does not contain estrogen. It works all day, every day, without you needing to remember anything. It does not protect against STIs or HIV, so use condoms too if there is any risk.
